meta.titre: The Human Digestive System: Organs, Enzymes and Common Disorders
meta.sous_theme: Alimentary canal, digestion, absorption and disorders

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Every afternoon in Douala, thousands of people eat rice, beans or ndole bought from a roadside stall. Within hours, that food has been broken down and carried into the blood to give energy for school and work. When the water or the food is not clean, the same digestive system can suffer from diarrhoea, which is a serious danger for young children. The GCE asks about the order of the organs, the work of enzymes and bile, and common digestive disorders, so each of these must be known precisely.

items: Food contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, mineral salts and water.
An enzyme is a protein that speeds up a chemical reaction in living things.
Digestion breaks large food molecules into small soluble molecules that can enter the blood.

sections.titre: Organs, digestive juices and the fate of food
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The alimentary canal in order
Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine (duodenum, jejunum and ileum), large intestine, rectum, anus. The liver, gall bladder and pancreas are associated organs: food does not pass through them.

| Organ | What happens there |
|---|---|
| Mouth | Teeth chew food (mechanical digestion). Saliva contains **salivary amylase**, which digests starch to maltose. |
| Oesophagus | Muscles push the food along by **peristalsis**, waves of contraction. |
| Stomach | Walls churn the food. Gastric juice has hydrochloric acid, which kills many bacteria, and **pepsin**, which begins the digestion of proteins. |
| Liver | Makes **bile**. |
| Gall bladder | Stores bile, which flows along the bile duct into the duodenum. |
| Pancreas | Makes pancreatic juice with amylase, protease and lipase. |
| Small intestine | Digestion is completed; most absorption takes place here. |
| Large intestine | Absorbs water and forms faeces. |
| Rectum and anus | Faeces are stored in the rectum and leave the body through the anus (egestion). |

### Bile
Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder. It contains **no enzymes**. It breaks large fat droplets into tiny droplets (**emulsification**), which gives lipase a larger surface to work on, and it neutralises the acid coming from the stomach.

### End products of digestion
Carbohydrates become glucose, proteins become amino acids, and fats become fatty acids and glycerol.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how the small intestine is adapted to absorb food
variantes.contenu_markdown: The inner wall has many finger-like **villi**, which give a very large surface area. Each villus has a wall only one cell thick, so food molecules pass through easily. A network of blood capillaries carries glucose and amino acids away, and a lymph vessel (the lacteal) takes up fatty acids and glycerol. The blood keeps moving, so the concentration of digested food next to the villus stays low, which helps absorption to continue.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes symptoms or asks for prevention
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- **Diarrhoea**: frequent, watery faeces, often caused by germs in dirty food or water. The body loses water and salts, so the person may become dehydrated. Treatment: drink plenty of clean fluids and oral rehydration solution. Prevention: boil or treat drinking water, wash hands, cover food.
- **Constipation**: faeces are retained in the rectum and become hard and dry, so they are passed with difficulty. It is linked to too little fibre and too little water. Prevention: eat fruits, vegetables and whole grains, drink water and take exercise.
- **Ulcer**: an open sore in the lining of the stomach or the duodenum.
- **Food poisoning**: vomiting and diarrhoea after eating food contaminated with germs.

sections.enonce_markdown: A child eats a piece of bread. Describe the journey of the bread through the alimentary canal, from the mouth to the anus, and state what happens to the starch and to the fibre. *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: "Describe the journey" calls for the organs in the right order, each with its action. Two things are asked about: starch and fibre.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
Teeth chew the bread; saliva with salivary amylase digests some starch to maltose.

etapes.justification: Peristalsis moves the food; acid and pepsin act on the proteins of the bread.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Peristalsis pushes the food to the stomach. The stomach churns it with gastric juice, in which pepsin begins the digestion of protein.

etapes.justification: Bile and pancreatic juice enter the duodenum; digestion is completed and food is absorbed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Pancreatic amylase and enzymes of the intestine change the remaining starch to glucose, which is absorbed through the villi into the blood.

etapes.justification: Fibre cannot be digested, so it is carried on with the rest of the waste.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Water is absorbed in the large intestine. The undigested fibre forms faeces, which are stored in the rectum and egested through the anus.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The bread is chewed in the mouth, where salivary amylase starts to change starch into maltose. It passes down the oesophagus by peristalsis to the stomach, where pepsin acts on protein. In the small intestine enzymes complete the digestion of starch to glucose, which is absorbed into the blood through the villi. The fibre is not digested; in the large intestine water is absorbed, and the faeces are stored in the rectum and leave through the anus.

items.erreur_markdown: "Bile digests fats because it is a strong enzyme."
items.pourquoi_faux: Bile contains no enzyme. It emulsifies fat into small droplets; the enzyme lipase does the chemical digestion.
items.correction_markdown: Bile emulsifies fat and neutralises acid; lipase digests fat to fatty acids and glycerol.

items.erreur_markdown: "Most digested food is absorbed in the large intestine."
items.pourquoi_faux: Most absorption takes place in the small intestine, through the villi. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.
items.correction_markdown: Small intestine: absorption of digested food. Large intestine: absorption of water.

items.erreur_markdown: "Digestion and absorption mean the same thing."
items.pourquoi_faux: Digestion is the breakdown of food into small soluble molecules. Absorption is the passage of those molecules into the blood.
items.correction_markdown: Digestion changes the food; absorption moves the end products into the blood.

items.pourquoi_faux: Faeces are food that was never digested and absorbed, so they were never part of the body's cells. Removing them is egestion. Excretion removes waste made by the body cells, such as urea.

items.enonce_markdown:
Match each organ with its function.

Organs: (a) liver, (b) pancreas, (c) large intestine, (d) oesophagus.

Functions: 1. absorbs water from undigested food; 2. makes bile; 3. carries food to the stomach by peristalsis; 4. makes a juice containing amylase, protease and lipase.

(a) For each food, name the enzyme that begins its digestion and the end product of its digestion: starch, protein, fat.
(b) A young child has severe watery diarrhoea. Explain why a nurse gives the child oral rehydration solution.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Starch: **amylase**, end product **glucose** (maltose is the first product). Protein: **pepsin** in the stomach, end product **amino acids**. Fat: **lipase**, end products **fatty acids and glycerol**.

(b) Diarrhoea makes the body lose a lot of water and salts quickly. The solution replaces the water and salts, which prevents or treats dehydration.

items.enonce_markdown:
A student sets up four test tubes. Each contains 5 cm$^3$ of starch solution and:

Tube A: 2 cm$^3$ of fresh saliva, kept at 37 $^\circ$C.
Tube B: 2 cm$^3$ of saliva that was boiled and cooled, kept at 37 $^\circ$C.
Tube C: 2 cm$^3$ of fresh saliva, kept in ice-cold water.
Tube D: 2 cm$^3$ of water, kept at 37 $^\circ$C.

After 15 minutes a drop from each tube is tested with iodine solution.

(a) State the total volume of liquid in each tube.
(b) State the colour expected in each tube, with a reason.
(c) Name the sugar formed in tube A and the test for it.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $5 + 2 = 7$, so each tube holds **7 cm$^3$**.

(b) Tube A: iodine stays **yellow-brown**, because salivary amylase at body temperature has digested the starch. Tube B: **blue-black**, because boiling destroyed the enzyme. Tube C: **blue-black** (or only a little paler), because the enzyme works very slowly at low temperature. Tube D: **blue-black**, because there is no enzyme; it is the control.

(c) **Maltose**. Heat a sample with Benedict's solution: a **brick-red (orange) precipitate** shows a reducing sugar.

items_markdown: Order of the canal: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus; liver, gall bladder and pancreas are associated organs.
Enzymes: amylase digests starch, pepsin and protease digest protein, lipase digests fat; end products are glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol.
Bile is made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder, has no enzymes, emulsifies fat and neutralises stomach acid.
Villi make the small intestine well adapted to absorption: large surface, thin wall, blood capillaries and a lacteal.
Diarrhoea causes loss of water and salts; constipation is retention of hard faeces in the rectum, helped by fibre and water.
Faeces are egested; excretion is the removal of waste made by body cells.
